subject: Retention of streamed tokens vs final responses — what gets stored by default
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-corp.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question — does streaming API persist partial tokens?

Hi Rishi,

Quick question from our security team: when we use Redwood's streaming endpoint, do you persist the intermediate/partial tokens (the stream fragments) anywhere, or only the final assembled response? Our compliance folks are specifically worried about PII appearing briefly in streaming fragments before we do client-side redaction.

Could you confirm what is stored by default (requests, streaming fragments, final responses, KV cache) and whether there are opt-outs for hosted customers? Appreciate a concise breakdown — legal is waiting.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Corp
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question — does streaming API persist partial tokens?

Samir — thanks for the clear note. Short answer up front: by default we DO NOT persist transient streaming fragments as first-class objects. We store the request payload and the final model output artifacts (assembled response) according to the hosted retention window. Details below: 

- What’s stored by default (hosted API):
  * Request payloads (user prompts / inputs): retained in logs for 45 days by default for debugging/quality and billing correlation.
  * Final responses (assembled model outputs, after the stream completes): retained for 45 days by default.
  * Streaming fragments (token-level partial chunks sent via SSE/HTTP2): not stored as separate, queryable artifacts. They are transient in the stream buffer and only materialize in persistent logs if the stream completes and the final response is recorded.
  * KV cache / runtime ephemeral state: not persisted to customer logs; exists in memory on serving nodes and is evicted per session.

- Opt-outs / controls for hosted customers:
  * We offer an account-level setting ("suppress_stream_logs") to avoid recording assembled final outputs — useful when customers want request-only retention or no retention at all.
  * Customers can also use client-side redaction (recommended) or pass a per-request header to instruct server-side redaction of specific fields.

I’ll loop in Kim (security) for formal language we can share with legal. 

—R
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-corp.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 31 May 2029 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question — does streaming API persist partial tokens?

Hi Samir — adding a bit of compliance-oriented detail.

1) Residency: the default retention window above applies within the region you select for the hosted instance. If Acme chooses eu-west region, artifacts remain in EU residency for the retention window.

2) Audit trail: we do record a small telemetry record for streaming sessions (session start/stop, error codes, byte counts) for operational troubleshooting. That telemetry does not contain token payloads by default.

3) Legal-safe option: for regulated workflows we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where you can set custom retention and ensure log sinks are customer-controlled. If you want us to draft a statement for your compliance team, we can provide an exportable data-flow diagram and a retention SLA excerpt. Attaching a short FAQ and a streaming data-flow image.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-corp.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 01 Jun 2029 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question — does streaming API persist partial tokens?

Samir — a couple of practical notes from the product side so you can operationalize this with your devs: 

- If you need zero retention for both requests and responses, toggle the account-level "no_persist" flag and we will stop writing those artifacts to our logs; you will still get billing events (token counts) but without payload content. This is supported for hosted customers with an addendum.
- For streaming clients: implement end-of-stream acknowledgment before storing anything on your side; avoid logging raw fragments client-side until acked.
- For customers who want shorter-than-default retention (e.g., 7 days), we can make a config change at the account level (subject to contract).

Let me know which option Acme prefers and we’ll propose a concise statement for legal.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Redwood Console
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 01 Jun 2029 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question — does streaming API persist partial tokens?

Thanks — this is helpful. Two quick clarifying items from legal: 1) when you say "assembled final outputs are retained", does that include any metadata that could reconstruct a partial stream (e.g., per-token timestamps)? 2) if we enable the "no_persist" flag, will we still be able to request audit logs that show the fact a request occurred (without payload)?

If you can provide exact wording for both, legal will sign off.

—Samir
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-corp.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 02 Jun 2029 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question — does streaming API persist partial tokens?

Samir — answers you can drop into legal: 

1) Metadata on final outputs: the stored final-response artifact contains timestamps for the request and the completion time, token counts, and model variant metadata. It does NOT contain per-token timestamp series or token-by-token offsets that would allow reconstruction of the streaming sequence.

2) "no_persist" / "suppress_stream_logs": enabling this will stop storage of payloads (requests and responses). We will continue to provide non-payload audit records (request id, timestamp, processing outcome, billing token counts) for the period required by billing reconciliation (default 90 days for non-payload billing receipts). Those audit records contain no textual payload.

Formal statement (copy/paste): "By default Redwood stores request payloads and assembled final responses for a 45-day window in the selected region. Streaming fragments are transient and not persisted as separate artifacts. If a customer enables a no_persist configuration, Redwood will cease storing payload content; non-payload audit records (request id, timestamps, processing outcome, token counts) remain available for billing and operational reconciliation without textual content."

If that looks good to Acme legal we can prepare an addendum and schedule a short 15-minute call to sign.

—Kim
